story.title: Story 5: Manual Smart Compact And PI Reload

result.reviewScopeSummary: Follow-up verification was limited to the two prior Story 5 blockers. I inspected the updated PI projection builder/writer, the new story-local integration/E2E suites, reran the prior manual system-role repro, ran the targeted Story 5 tests, and reran `npm run verify` plus `npm run verify-all`. I also checked the upstream PI message/session type contracts to determine whether the new system-role output is actually native-format-safe.

priorFindingStatuses.rationale: The prior downcast bug is fixed at the project level: the manual repro now produces `file.entries[0].role === "system"` and a written JSONL message with `message.role === "system"`, and new unit tests cover both builder and writer system-role handling. However, the writer now achieves this by emitting a `role: "system"` payload through `message as unknown as SessionMessageEntry["message"]`, while the upstream local PI contracts inspected during verification still declare `Message = UserMessage | AssistantMessage | ToolResultMessage` and only extend `AgentMessage` with `custom`, `bashExecution`, `branchSummary`, and `compactionSummary`. I cannot establish from current evidence whether `role: "system"` is truly part of PI’s native session-file format or whether preserving system-origin source metadata requires a different representation. That is now a native-format contract question rather than a straightforward implementation bug.

The story-local deep coverage now exists and runs. `tests/thread-view/pi-thread-view-writer.integration.test.ts`, `tests/commands/smart-compact.integration.test.ts`, and `tests/commands/smart-compact.e2e.test.ts` are present, are discovered by the test runners, and passed in the targeted Story 5 run as well as `npm run verify-all`. The new suites exercise the real file-backed write/archive/load path and the smart-compact command loop over real stores.

openFindings.title: System-role preservation is now implemented via an unproven PI native-format contract
openFindings.evidence: `src/thread-view/targets/pi/pi-thread-view-builder.ts:72-98` now preserves `piRole/rawType === "system"`, and `src/thread-view/targets/pi/pi-thread-view-writer.ts:323-377` serializes a `{ role: "system" }` message and forces it through `message as unknown as SessionMessageEntry["message"]`. The previous manual repro now writes a JSONL entry with `message.role: "system"`. But the upstream contracts inspected locally still define `Message = UserMessage | AssistantMessage | ToolResultMessage` in `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/types.d.ts:139-167`, extend `AgentMessage` only with `custom`, `bashExecution`, `branchSummary`, and `compactionSummary` in `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/messages.d.ts:32-58`, and type `SessionMessageEntry.message` as `AgentMessage` in `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/session-manager.d.ts:23-25`. The new integration/E2E tests use a harness double that switches to the file path but does not parse or validate session message roles, so they do not prove that `role: "system"` is accepted by PI as native session content.

unverified: Whether `role: "system"` is actually valid PI-native session-file content for `SessionMessageEntry.message` rather than a project-local extension that needs a different representation

productionPathFindings: The production writer now preserves system-origin source metadata by emitting `role: "system"` session messages, but that shape is not declared in the locally inspected upstream PI message/session contracts, so native-format safety for this path remains unproven.
openQuestions: Does PI’s real native session-file contract intentionally allow `SessionMessageEntry.message.role === "system"`, or should Story 5 preserve system-origin source metadata some other way that stays inside the upstream `AgentMessage` contract?
additionalObservations: The missing deep-coverage blocker from the previous verifier pass is closed: the new story-local integration and E2E suites exist, are discovered by the runners, and passed.

`custom` role handling now aligns with the upstream coding-agent extension contract; the remaining ambiguity is specific to raw system-role projection, not to custom messages or the archive/load command path.
